phrase: a copy of the given array after sorting
text: sort the given array itself, then return a copy of the sorted array; the given array is changed by the call, which contradicts R-MUT-1 (don't change the given array)

phrase: first index value, last index value
text: the indices themselves: 0 + (len(array) - 1), so the sum is len(array) - 1 and its parity depends only on the length (both examples are also consistent with this reading)

phrase: the sum( first index value, last index value)
text: the first and last values of the sorted copy, i.e. min(array) + max(array), which is the same for either sort order (both examples are also consistent with this reading)
odd only: ascending exactly when the parity sum is odd; 'or even' is a slip (matches examples R-EX-3 and R-EX-4 and makes the rule complementary to the even case of R-ORD-2)
strictly increasing: duplicates removed, which contradicts R-RET-2 (the result is a copy with the same elements)

phrase: you will sort the given array
text: sort the given array itself, in place; this contradicts R-MUT-1 (don't change the given array)
even only: descending exactly when the parity sum is even; 'or odd' is a slip (matches examples R-EX-3 and R-EX-4 and makes the rule complementary to the odd case of R-ORD-1)
strictly decreasing: duplicates removed, which contradicts R-RET-2 (the result is a copy with the same elements)
'it' is the given array itself, sorted in place; this contradicts R-MUT-1 (don't change the given array)
